body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: 5xx spike detected on private inference gateway (gw-private-01). Error rate 5xx -> 6.8% over last 5m, latency up, automated alerts triggered. Affected: private/VPC customers in us-west-2 peering. Paging oncall.
sarah: acknowledged, paging oncall now. checked datadog dashboard — spike aligns with increased connection resets to gw-private-01.
mike: I'm oncall. seeing 502/504s and timeouts for a subset of private customers. can anyone confirm recent infra changes?
jordan: I saw a small firewall rule push ~12:43 UTC that tightened egress to peering appliance from 10.0.32.0/24 -> allowed ports only 443,80. Could be related.
ashley: we did a config change to remove a legacy broad egress SG earlier as cleanup. change id sg-pt-cleanup-2026. Was supposed to be safe but might have clipped ephemeral ports.
mike: timeline: alert at 12:47, firewall change at 12:43. logs show lots of TCP RST from peering-gw and client side FINs. suspect NAT sessions failing over. Jordan can you run conntrack dump on gw-private-01?
jordan: running now. output snippet: 
```
# conntrack -L | grep gw-private-01 | head -n 5
udp      17 src=10.0.32.45 dst=34.200.1.2 sport=50000 dport=443 packets=120 bytes=15000 src=34.200.1.2 dst=52.10.10.5 sport=443 dport=50000 packets=120 bytes=14800
tcp      6 src=10.0.32.78 dst=34.200.1.2 sport=50010 dport=443 state=ESTABLISHED src=34.200.1.2 dst=52.10.10.6 sport=443 dport=50010
tcp      6 src=10.0.32.78 dst=34.200.1.2 sport=50010 dport=443 state=FIN_WAIT src=34.200.1.2 dst=52.10.10.6 sport=443 dport=50010
```
```
Noticing duplicate mappings: multiple internal sessions mapped to same external ephemeral port (50010) — looks like SNAT collision/duplication on the peering appliance.
```
mike: SNAT collisions would explain asymmetric packets and 5xx on backend. Any recent NAT scaling or peering appliance config change?
jordan: peering appliance autoscaler did a drain/scale around 12:42 due to load; it re-attached NAT pool but seems to have reused ephemeral port allocations without flushing conntrack entries. Also firewall change removed ephemeral-range health exceptions so new sessions couldn't complete TCP handshake to the peer, leaving half-open entries.
ashley: confirmed we removed egress rule that allowed 32768-60999 ephemeral range to peering appliance. That was meant for legacy infra. I can revert.
mike: revert it and monitor. also add temporary ACL to send traffic to hosted fallback pool for impacted customers. we should divert to hosted cluster to reduce customer 5xx.
sarah: I'm messaging customer success with a short blurb: "We are investigating elevated errors for some private deployments in us-west-2. Engineers are mitigating; we'll update in 10 min."
jordan: patching SG to re-open ephemeral range now. command: 
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-xxxx --protocol tcp --port 32768-60999 --cidr 10.0.32.0/24
```
applied at 12:51 UTC.
mike: rolling routing change to point impacted routes to hosted fallback model (route-tag: fallback-hosted-usw2) — deploying canary for 10% of traffic. config snippet: 
```
redwood-routectl set-route --service inference-gw --selector private=customerA --weight 90:private,10:hosted-fallback-usw2
```
applied at 12:53.
ashley: SG revert confirmed. conntrack shows fewer duplicate mappings now. but still seeing some mid-flight 504s from clients.
jordan: forcing conntrack conn flush for stale entries on gw-private-01 for impacted source subnet: 
```
conntrack -D --orig-src 10.0.32.0/24
```
executed 12:55. note: this will briefly drop some in-flight connections.
mike: ok proceed. We should see error rate drop after flush + SG reopen + routing fallback. Also kicking up infra logging for deeper traces: tcpdump on gw-private-01 to capture abnormal resets.
sarah: customer update posted: "Mitigation in progress: engineers reverted a network rule and are routing a small portion of traffic to a hosted fallback to reduce errors. We expect improvement within ~10 minutes."
ashley: tcpdump captured pattern: backend responds but NAT translates to same ephemeral port for multiple internal IPs, then responses land on wrong origin -> client times out then gateway returns 502. possible double-SNAT scenario with peering appliance acting as middle SNAT and also our gateway doing SNAT.
jordan: checking NAT behavior on peering appliance: looks like it re-applied an older NAT table after scale event. opening a ticket with peering vendor but in parallel we'll modify our gateway to preserve source port where possible (enable `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` constraints and source port preservation).
mike: action list: 1) ashley reopened SG ephemeral range (done), 2) jordan flushed conntrack and confirmed reduction (done), 3) mike routed 10% to hosted fallback (done), 4) increase logging and tcpdump capture (in progress), 5) oncall-l2 to take over monitoring and post regular updates.
oncall-l2: taking over for monitoring and customer comms. I'll keep watch for next 30m and escalate to netops if error rate >= 3% for 10m.
sarah: initial metrics: 5xx dropped from 6.8% -> 2.1% within 6m after actions. latency p95 improving.
mike: nice. I'll hand this to netops for root cause and long-term fix (prevent double-SNAT and ensure ephemeral ranges preserved on peering autoscale). oncall-l2, ping me if it regresses. I'm out for next 20m but available by ping.
netops-bot: created ticket NETOPS-4482 "Peering appliance NAT port reuse on autoscale causing SNAT collisions" assigned to jordan. Link: https://tracker.redwood.ai/NETOPS-4482
netops-bot: paging oncall-netops schedule for follow-up.
oncall-l2: acknowledged. adding runbook steps to incident doc and will post postmortem template. customers updated: sent follow-up note with ETA for RCA in 24-48h.
sarah: closing active paging loop unless new alerts. leaving thread for netops RCA and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
